text:
alex kim: Quick follow-up from the RFC review - we need a pragmatic pattern for job/background-worker auth that preserves least-privilege and traceability. Thoughts?

maria gonzalez: Agree. Main tradeoff: fully-scoped per-job API keys vs a delegated short-lived token minted by an operator service. Per-key is simple but explosion + rotation pain. :grimacing:

samir patel: Can we do a hybrid? Operator mints short-lived actor tokens with an actor_id that maps to project/org and intent. Jobs use that token only for specific routes.

jin park: Hybrid sounds good. Must ensure auditability: every request needs x-actor-id and x-token-origin metadata in traces/logs. We can piggyback on existing request header forwarding.

alex kim: Example mint flow I sketched:
POST /mint-actor-token
{ service: "batcher", job_type: "ingest-daily", project: "proj-123" }
-> returns { token: short_jwt, expires_in: 3600, actor_id: "svc-batcher:proj-123:ingest-daily" }
Job uses Authorization: Bearer short_jwt. Runtime validates signature + checks binding to actor_id and route scope.

maria gonzalez: Important: signed tokens should carry capability claims not raw role ids. e.g., cap: ["read:datasets:proj-123", "write:checkpoints:proj-123"] so runtime doesn't need RBAC graph lookups for every request. Cache TTLs for policy checks.

samir patel: We must guard mint endpoint: only operator services with elevated rights can mint. That's where an operator-level service identity (long-lived, rotated infrequently) issues ephemeral tokens. Also rate-limit and require 2PC approval for high-scope tokens.

jin park: Ops-bot: can you add an alerting rule for unusual mint rates?

ops-bot: alert created: operator.mint.rate > 50/min for 5m -> #eng-security + oncall.

alex kim: Edge-case: what about chained delegation (service A calls B on behalf of job)? Two options: propagate original actor token or mint a new delegated token that includes provenance (actor_id, parent_token_id). I prefer explicit delegation token to avoid full-scope propagation.

maria gonzalez: Agreed. Delegation tokens allow truncated caps: parent token might have ingest:*, child gets ingest:dataset-x. Also helps traceability.

samir patel: Implementation note: keep tokens compact for TLS header size limits. Encode claims as short keys, e.g., c:[r:d:p-123] and expand server-side.

jin park: Migration plan (quick sketch):
- Phase 1: operator mint service + support short-lived actor tokens; runtime accepts either long-lived API keys or short tokens.
- Phase 2: require actor headers and ban raw long-lived keys for new routes; add telemetry.
- Phase 3: rotate old long-lived keys off, enforce delegation token for cross-service calls.

alex kim: Can someone draft a small RFC addendum with the mint API, token claim schema, and runtime validation pseudocode? Keep it < 2 pages.

maria gonzalez: I'll take the addendum. Will include sample JWT claim set and validation flow.

samir patel: I'll prototype a mint service shim and sample policy cache behavior.

jin park: I'll draft the alerting + logging requirements and add the header forwarding bits to the tracing integration.

alex kim: Cool. Action items pinned: @maria gonzalez (RFC addendum), @samir patel (mint prototype), @jin park (telemetry+alerts). Revisit in 1 week. :thumbsup:

maria gonzalez: One more callout - encryption of tokens at rest in job queues (SQS/kafka) is mandatory. Jobs should fetch token from a local secret store at start and not keep in logs.

samir patel: Noted. Will add encrypt-in-queue: true to prototyping checklist.

jin park: Also add a small test plan for replay attempts: tokens must include nonce and short TTL + nbf so replay window is tiny.

alex kim: Thanks all. We'll sync next Tuesday.
